correctness.rationale: A deterministic booster interval induces a uniform stationary vaccine-age distribution; direct integration of sigma(a)=min(a/tau,1) yields F(x)=1-x/2 for x<=1 and F(x)=1/(2x) for x>=1. For the purely cross-group contact matrix, the positive Perron root squared is F(x)F(B-x). A complete algebraic four-regime analysis shows corner-only minima for B<2, all allocations equal to 1/4 at B=2, and a unique equal split for B>2. Equality cases and boundary B=1 are checked explicitly. The accompanying stdlib Fraction program passed 121840 finite checks; the inequalities prove all real feasible allocations. Scope is disease-free rate and linear invasion, not endemic dynamics.

originality.rationale: In the inspected journal model, Proposition 6 proves fair vaccine allocation for contact-mixing alpha at most one and does not cover purely cross-group mixing alpha two. The general spectral matrix is prior art, but the global budget-dependent argmin trichotomy, all-split neutrality at the critical budget, and exact lower envelope for deterministic boosters under linearly waning susceptibility were not found in searched papers or published records. Prior-art priority is qualified and not a certified uniqueness assertion.
residual_risks: An unlocated general theorem on optimal products of renewal susceptibilities could specialize to this result, even without matching terminology.
The profile is an idealized, deliberately simple clipped-linear waning curve and the mixing matrix is a bipartite endpoint; neither broad applicability nor real policy preference is claimed.
The optimality addresses linear invasion, not nonlinear long-term infection burden.
No independent scientific validation or exhaustive global literature certification has been performed.

value.rationale: In the precise fully disassortative regime outside the motivating assortative-fairness theorem, the exact global optimizer changes sharply from complete concentration under vaccine scarcity to fair allocation above the vaccine-waning timescale. At the threshold all allocations are genuinely equally optimal. This supplies a complete interpretable nontrivial phase diagram and a calibrated benchmark contrasting booster schedule laws; it is not merely a restatement of Jensen, a numerical example or a bare parameter substitution.
